Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
Thanks, operator. Thank you for joining us today to discuss our Q1 2025 earnings results. Joining me on the call today are Mr. Leaf Li, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Arthur Chen, Chief Financial Officer, and Robin Xu, Senior Vice President. As a reminder, today's call may include forward-looking statements, which represent the company's belief regarding future events, which, by their nature, are not certain and are outside of the company's control. Forward-looking statements involving inherent risks and uncertainties. We caution you that a number of important factors could cause actual results to differ materially from those containing any forward-looking statements. For more information about the potential risks and uncertainties, please refer to the company's filings with the SEC, including its annual report. With that, I will now turn the call over to Leaf. Leaf will make his comments in Chinese. I will translate.
Thank you all for joining our earnings call today. We kicked off 2025 with strong momentum, adding approximately 262,000 new funded accounts in Q1, up 48% year-over-year and 22% quarter-over-quarter. By quarter end, total funded accounts stood at 2.7 million, a 42% increase from a year ago and an 11% rise sequentially. With a third of our annual target already in the bag, we are tracking well against our guidance of 800,000 net new funded accounts in 2025. For Q2 in a row, Hong Kong market led in new funded accounts amid a risk-on mood for China equities. An active IPO calendar also helped acquire new clients while reactivating previously dormant ones.
We believe that brokers with strong brand equity, seamless user experience, and superior execution capabilities are best positioned to convert market tailwinds into sustained growth. Funded account growth in the US picked up pace as we enhanced the platform experience for active traders. Our Take Charge of Your Trading campaign in New York City also boosted brand visibility and deepened engagement with retail investors. Malaysia delivered the fastest sequential growth in new funded accounts across all seven markets, fueled by effective marketing campaigns and our seamless Malaysian IPO subscription experience. Looking ahead, we still see significant runway for market share expansion and remain committed to product localization and brand investment. In Japan, new funded accounts saw strong sequential growth and reached a historic high, reaffirming our position as the preferred platform for US equity trading among Japanese retail investors.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
Among the products we shipped in Q1, the highlight was Futubull AI, a smart investment assistant trained on Futu's proprietary financial data and investor community insights. This integrated solution combines AI-powered search, Q&A, and customer support, offering context-aware responses tailored to retail investors. Since launch, it has received overwhelmingly positive feedback with a satisfaction rate of around 90% and has demonstrated significantly higher accuracy and professionalism in answering investment-related questions than general-purpose models. We plan to roll out similar AI offerings to other international markets in Q2 to empower investors globally.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
In Q1, we also launched a brand new desktop version of Futubull, built on a new framework compatible with Windows, macOS, and Linux. This next-generation version features intuitive drag-and-drop tools for building quantitative strategies and enumerates multi-leg option strategies that reflect clients' views on the securities, bringing institutional-grade functionalities in a more user-friendly manner. In Japan, we introduced US fractional shares trading in February to enhance accessibility, followed by the April launch of US options trading to help clients better capture market movements.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
Total client assets reached HKD 830 billion, marking a 60% increase year-over-year and a 12% increase quarter-over-quarter. The growth was primarily driven by record net asset inflow. The rally of Hong Kong equities, led by large cap tech names, drove significant asset inflow. Total client assets in Singapore rose 11% sequentially, marking the 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, thanks to robust inflow into US equities and wealth management products. In Canada and Australia, average client assets increased for the fifth consecutive quarter, underscoring improving client quality and growing brand trust. Margin financing and securities lending balance closed the quarter at HKD 50.3 billion, largely stable from the prior quarter as clients delevered in March amid market pullback.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
Total trading volume reached HKD 3.22 trillion in Q1, up 140% year-over-year and 11% quarter-over-quarter. US equity trading rose 8% sequentially to HKD 2.25 trillion, supported by bottom fishing of semiconductor and technology stocks. Trading volume in Hong Kong equities advanced 21% quarter-over-quarter to HKD 916 billion, lifted by a resurgence in investor sentiment amid the DeepSeek-induced rally. In the US, we saw double-digit sequential growth in both the number of options traders and the number of options contracts traded, with the latter reaching a historic high.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
Wealth management client assets reached HKD 139.2 billion as of quarter-end, up 118% year-over-year and 26% quarter-over-quarter. 29% of funded accounts held wealth management products, a further sequential increase. A big part of the inflow was driven by money market funds as clients flocked to safe haven assets amid market volatility. At the same time, we saw rising allocations into bond funds and strong demand for structured notes, especially in Singapore. In Hong Kong and Singapore, we expanded our structured product lineup with FX-linked nodes. In Malaysia, we onboarded equity funds, while in Japan, we rolled out US dollar-denominated money market funds to better serve clients' cash management needs. Next, I'd like to invite our CFO, Arthur, to discuss our financial performance.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Leaf Li, Daniel Yuan. Please allow me to walk you through our financial performance in Q1. All the numbers are in HKD unless otherwise noted. Total revenue was HKD 4.7 billion, up 81% from HKD 2.6 billion in Q1 2024. Brokerage commission and handling charge income was HKD 2.3 billion, an increase of 113% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter. The year-over-year increase was mainly driven by higher trading volume, partially offset by the decline in blended commission rate. The year-over-year decline in blended commission rate was mainly driven by changes in product mix and a higher average order size for Hong Kong stock trading. The quarter-over-quarter increase was mainly driven by the sequential growth in trading volume.
Interest income was $2.1 billion, up 53% year-over-year and 2% quarter-over-quarter. The year-over-year increase was driven by high interest income from security borrowing and the lending business, margin financing, and the bank deposits. The quarter-over-quarter increase was driven by higher margin financing income, as well as higher interest income from security borrowing and the lending business, partially offset by lower interest income from bank deposits due to lower interest rate on clients' cash deposits. Other income was $314 million, up 101% year-over-year and down 11% quarter-over-quarter. The year-over-year increase was primarily attributable to higher fund distribution service income and the currency exchange income.
Our total cost was HKD 749 million, an increase of 59% from HKD 417 million in Q1 2024. Brokerage commission and the handling charge expenses was HKD 144 million, up 138% year-over-year, and 28% quarter-over-quarter. Both the year-over-year and the quarter-over-quarter increase was roughly in line with the movement of our brokerage commission and handling charge income. Interest expenses were HKD 469 million, up 50% year-over-year and down 9% quarter-over-quarter. The year-over-year increase was driven by higher interest expenses associated with our security borrowing and the lending business and a higher margin financing interest expenses. The quarter-over-quarter decrease was mainly due to lower margin financing interest expenses and the lower interest expenses associated with our security borrowing and the lending business.
Processing and the servicing costs were $136 million, up 44% and down 10% Q over Q. The year-over-year increase was largely due to higher market information data fee for enhanced market data coverage, and the Q over Q decline was mainly driven by lower system usage fee, as well as lower market information and data fees. As a result, our total gross profit was $3.9 billion, an increase of 86% from $2.1 billion in Q1 2024. Gross margin was 84% as compared to 81.9% in Q1 2024. Operating expenses were up 36% year-over-year and down 12% Q over Q to $1.3 billion. R&D expenses were $386 million, up 15% year-over-year and down 3% Q over Q.
The year-over-year increase was primarily driven by investing AI capabilities and the related technology initiatives. The Q-over-Q decline was mainly due to the sequential decrease in R&D headcounts. Selling and the marketing expenses were HKD 459 million, up 57% year-over-year and down 1% Q-over-Q. The year-over-year increase was roughly in line with.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
The growth of our new fund accounts. The Q-over-Q decrease was mainly due to lower client acquisition costs, partially offset by the sequential increase in new funded accounts. G&A expenses were $415 billion, up 38% year-over-year and down 28% Q-over-Q. The year-over-year increase was primarily due to increase in the general administrative headcount to support overseas market development, and the Q-over-Q decrease was mainly due to bonus accrual for general administrative personnel in the previous quarter. As a result, income from operations increased 125% year-over-year and 21% Q-over-Q to $2.7 billion. Operating margin increased to 57.2% from 46% in Q1 2024, mostly due to strong top-line growth and operating leverage.
Our net income increased by 107% year-over-year and 15% Q-over-Q to HKD 2.1 billion. Net income margin expanded to 45.6% in Q1 as compared to 39.9% in the same quarter last year. Our effective tax rate for the quarter was 18.6%. That conclude our prepared remarks. We'd now like to open the call to questions. Operator, please go ahead. Thank you.
Operator

One moment for the first question. First question comes from Cindy Wang of China Renaissance. Please go ahead.

Director, China Renaissance

I have two questions here. First, the overall Hong Kong and US stock market fluctuated greatly in April and May. Could you give us some color on the trading velocity, trading volume, and the margin financing security lending balance on your platform so far in Q2? Second question is, recently we see Futubull and the moomoo launch membership program. Could you let us know what the business model looks like for this program and how many paying clients have already subscribed these services? Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]
[Foreign Language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
The new funded accounts in Q2 will probably see double-digit sequential decrease sequentially, mostly due to a very high base on Q1. Overall, we maintain very strong client acquisition momentum in Q2, and we are very confident to hit our 800,000 new paying clients guidance for 2025. With very big market volatility, clients continue to trade very actively. Based on the current run rate, we expect a further sequential increase in total trading volume. Clients also deposit a lot of assets into our platform quarter-to-date based on the run rate. Net asset inflow will stay at a very high level, similar to what we saw in Q1.
Coupled with some mark-to-market positive impact since the second half of April due to the market rebound, we expect a further sequential lift to our total client assets. Thank you.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
In terms of the membership programs we've launched recently, it is more catered to our wealth management products clients, particularly for these clients with huge assets or higher trading velocity, or even have some particular risk appetite, into some alternative, you know, wealth management products. We will start to layer different clients, in terms of their risk appetite, their current assets, and different product needs. Given, we just launched the programs recently, the penetration and the absolute number of these membership clients, versus our total clients, the proportion is still very small. Thank you.

Thank you for the questions. One moment for the next questions. Our next question comes from Charles Zhou from UBS. Please go ahead.
[Foreign Language]
[Translator 2]

Um, so first of all, congratulations to the management.
I think it's a very strong set of results and beat the consensus and also our estimate. I have two questions. The first one, could you please maybe just give us, you know, a little bit more colors about the timeline of your crypto trading business? And also the implication of the passage of the Hong Kong Stablecoins Bill recently, you know, to your company. The second question is about, can we talk about the customer retention and also the client AUM following the rising, you know, recent concern over the taxation on Mainland China clients' overseas investment income. Thank you.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]
[Foreign Language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
The crypto prices experienced some pullback, since Q1, that affected the enthusiasm of the crypto investors on our platform. The monthly trading volume and the number of crypto traders stayed at a pretty high level. Since May, the crypto prices rebounded, and we've seen investors quickly picked up interest in crypto trading. We also saw a rebound in daily trading volume. We'll continue to build crypto related product capabilities.
Recently, we launched the crypto deposit functionalities in Hong Kong, which made it easier for our clients to seamlessly deposit the crypto onto Futu's platform, and make it easy to switch between different asset classes. After we launched this function, we got very good feedback from the Web3 community and also very positive feedback from our clients. We plan to launch crypto withdrawal functions very soon.
We also launched the crypto paper trading function in Hong Kong, and we're the first regulated crypto platform to allow for paper trading, which really helps the newbie investors to familiarize themselves with the trading rules and the trading procedures, especially during market volatility. A couple of days ago, we launched crypto trading on a Grayscale basis and in most of the states in the United States, and we now support over 30 mainstream cryptocurrency trading. We'll closely monitor our clients trading behaviors to iterate on our product, and we plan to increase the number of cryptocurrencies in the near future. From a long-term perspective, we are very bullish about virtual assets as an asset class. For Futu, the take rate for crypto trading is higher than cash equities.
We believe that as if the regulatory landscape and the regulatory guidelines becoming more clear, there will be more cryptocurrency allowed and more functions allowed, which will bring Futu more ways to monetize from this asset class. We believe that whether it's from an AUM or revenue perspective, crypto has so much potential and we are still in the very, very early innings. In terms of stablecoins, we are aware of the relevant regulations being released recently. Airstar Bank, invested by Futu, participates in the stablecoin sandbox and exploring ways to do stablecoin custody. Thank you.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
Now many countries in the world have participated in this Common Reporting System. For the countries that participate in the Common Reporting System, the CRS rules apply to all of the licensed financial institutions, whether it's banks or insurance companies or brokers. There is a very clear set of rules that is executed consistently across different financial intermediaries. Although United States is not part of CRS, it has its own FATCA system, which established this tax information exchange mechanism with most of the mainstream countries in the world. As all of the other licensed brokers in Hong Kong, without the explicit request from the Hong Kong SFC, and if it's not compliant with the relevant laws and regulations of Hong Kong, Futu Securities will not disclose client information and client data to any third parties.
We've noticed that on the internet there have been some rumors about Futu disclosing client data and client trading information to third parties. We want to wanna make sure that everyone knows that these are very baseless rumors. We always adhere to regulatory requirements. We want our clients to also correctly and understand and interpret these laws and regulations. We've actually done a lot of education in this area as well. So far, we have not seen this leading to meaningful client attrition and asset outflow. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you for the question. One moment for the next question. Our next question comes from the line of Emma Xu of Bank of America Securities. Please go ahead.
Emma Xu
Greater China and FinTech Research Analyst, Bank of America
[Foreign Language]
[Translator 1]
Translator 1
Congratulations on another quarter of outstanding performance. I have a question regarding HIBOR. Recently, the HIBOR dropped sharply. How will this impact your net interest income?
Meanwhile, with HIBOR falling, are we seeing changes in client behavior such as increased fund deposits and more allocation to money market fund equity asset, or more active trading? Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]。 In our last earning call actually we provide a sensitive analysis assume, you know, every 25 basis rate cut or pre-tax monthly pre-tax profit will be down HKD 8 to 10 million roughly.
[Foreign Language]
Since the Fed rate cut last year by 50 basis points, we see the overall interest income revenues in Q1 continue to grow on a quarter-over-quarter basis, which is mainly because the average size of our idle cash balance largely offset the rate cut implications. At the same time, as you mentioned, the recent declines in HIBOR, which will trigger more clients' trading activities in terms of velocity, and consequently we will benefit from the trading commissions. On the other hand, we think the recent sharp declines by HIBOR may be just a temporary, partially due to certain mega IPOs in Hong Kong. Whether it will be sustained in such a low level, it is still wait to see. Thank you.

Charles Zhu
Executive Director, Morgan Stanley

[Translator 2]

What's the outlook for the full year? Second question is about if any quantitative metrics that we can look at, to measure the adoption or engagement satisfaction and client stickiness, arising from the AI tools that we have launched. What could potentially, could be done more in this space? Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]。In terms of the Q1 net asset inflows, actually we see a very strong inflow momentum across our seven different markets.
The overall asset inflow by the group increased over 50% quarter-over-quarter basis. As Leaf mentioned in the opening remarks, it is our record high in a single quarter numbers. In terms of the geographic breakdowns, Hong Kong and Singapore still are the majority contributor markets for the asset inflows. Going forward, we are constructively positive on the overall on the full year asset inflow situation. Thank you.
[Foreign Language]
We've launched the Futubull AI functions for about two months now. It's not been that long. We're still analyzing more data. Based on the preliminary numbers we have seen, our users have very good feedback of our Futubull AI function, and that also leads to more engagement and activity on our platform. We've also packaged our AI functions into our membership programs. There's a limited number of free questions you could ask to AI, and that depends on the tier of your membership. That is based on the client assets and the trading behavior on our platform, which means that the AI function has helped with net asset inflow and the trading velocity.
I think that's why we're trying to roll out AI functions to more international markets based on the initial traction we have seen of our Hong Kong clients. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you for the question. Just one moment for the next question. Next question comes from Yuan Fang of CICC. Please go ahead.
Yuan Fang
Equity Research Analyst, CICC

[Translator 1]

Uh, this is You Yuan Fang from CICC, and I have two questions here.
The first one is about the customer acquisition cost, the CAC. We see it decline much this quarter. What's the reason behind? Do you have any new guidance for the future CAC? The second question is that we have announced to entry the new New Zealand market. Would you please share more color on this market?
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]。 In terms of the CAC, in Q1, the average CAC we reached around, in Q1 is around HKD 1,800, which is relatively lower than our objectives in the beginning of this year, partially due to a very strong market tailwinds we got, regardless in China, the China assets re-rating, very strong IPO markets in Hong Kong and volatilities in the US.
In these trading windows, our marketing colleagues, you know, timely catch these windows, and thanks to our brand equities, influence as well, we got a very good result. Going forward, we do expect, you know, we will continue to set client growth as our first priority. At the same time, we will further emphasize our brand building, you know, deployment, in terms of the fundings. In the long run, we think, you know, the further enhance of the brand equity will, you know, let us become more resilient in different trading investment cycles. The investment on this brand equity, the effect in the near term, it is very difficult to predict.
Not to mention the overall market environments and the macro environment is still include a lot of uncertainties. From the prudence angles, we will maintain our full year guidance on CAC unchanged, but we will revisit this assumption in the coming quarters.
Thank you.
[Foreign Language]，for the second question regarding the，uh，blended，uh，blended commission rate changes。Actually there, there are some-Slightly uptick, uh, on a Q on Q basis, uh, 在 terms of the blended, uh, blended commission rate.
The reason behind that is mainly due to the product, the mix change. There's more clients trading on certain derivatives such as, you know, US options, etc. Going forward, as we will launch more new products, for instance, the crypto trading, etc., I do expect that our overall blended commission rate will maintain stable. Thank you.

Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
Thank you for the question. One moment for the next question. Our next question comes from Allen Wang from Citi. Please go ahead.
Allen Wang
Equity Research Analyst, Citi
Allen Wang from Citi. Thanks management for giving me the chance to ask a question. This is Allen from Citibank. My first question is on Hong Kong markets. Futu previously has a market share target about 40% in Hong Kong, that basically implies about 1 million paying customers in Hong Kong.
Judging from our Q1 numbers, our paying customer numbers is already approaching close to around 900,000. Given the pace of our new paying customer acquisition in Hong Kong is so fast, we think our long-term goal of market share of 40% in Hong Kong is probably within reach within the next couple of quarters. Against this backdrop, wondering if management could share your updated view on the Hong Kong markets, especially considering that there's recent changes in the competitive landscape with potential competition for Ant Group and Robinhood. If we look beyond the 40% market share, how much additional headroom do we see to further increase market share in Hong Kong? The second question is on interest income.
We see that the idle cash balance has grown very notably during Q1. Wondering if management could help us break down the interest income, how much of that is coming from idle cash, and how much of that is from margin finances, security lending, etc?
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]. in terms for the second question regarding the idle cash, roughly, you know, the idle cash related income account for 35% to 40% of our total interest income for this quarter. The very strong robust increase in the revenue arising from idle cash partially due to two reasons. Number one is, we got a very strong net asset inflows from, you know, existing clients, not to mention a lot of new clients we acquire in the Q1. Secondly, is due to the market was quite volatile in the Q1. In our observation, a lot of clients actually, you know, partially inclined to increase their cash position and lower their stock positions. Which is, you know, we got some benefit of arising from that as well. Thank you. Over to you.
Leaf Hua Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
In terms of our Hong Kong market share, the absolute number of fund accounts you mentioned applies to our Greater China business, while the market share target you mentioned was about our Hong Kong local business. These two numbers are not apple-to-apple comparisons. In the past two quarters, we have seen the Hong Kong market contributed the highest number of paying clients among all of our seven markets, which gave us confidence that as a leading broker in Hong Kong, we'll be able to gain outsized benefits from favorable market conditions. We think that our Hong Kong business has huge runway for growth, first, both in terms of client numbers and client assets. The Hong Kong market has never been short of competition.
In the past few years, there have been a number of our peers, very notable peers entering into Hong Kong. Regardless how the outside market environment changes, we've always been doing product innovation and product iteration, and we believe that our product capabilities have built a very strong barrier to entry for our business. In each and every market we enter into, we build very customized product experience, very innovative product features. Coupled with our superior user experience and very competitive pricing strategy, we continue to gain user mind share in Hong Kong and take market share. On top of that, we think brand is probably one of the most important intangible assets of financial services platform, and building a brand takes time.
Futu has built a considerable level of trust with our clients, and we've seen very, very high client stickiness on our platform. It's consistently above 98%, 99% on a quarterly basis. If there is a newcomer that cannot provide highly differentiated product experience and service, we don't think it can sway the client choices. As we continue to build our brand, we also see a higher number of high net worth clients in Hong Kong, which contributed to a very high net asset inflow quarter-over-quarter. We've also seen that when the clients choose a broker, that decision is usually multidimensional, whether it's, you know, applying a zero commission strategy or just to direct traffic from other platforms. We don't think either one is gonna achieve very desirable effects.
The users will choose the platforms that are compliant, that have high brand recognition, and have the strongest all-rounded capabilities. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you for the questions. Our last question comes from Zoey Zong from Jefferies. Please go ahead.
Zoey Zong
Senior Associate of China Internet and Media, Jefferies
[Foreign Language].Thanks management for taking my questions, and congratulations on your solid results. I have two questions. Firstly, I have a follow-up question on Futubull AI. Management mentioned that more AI products will be launched in overseas markets in Q2. Wondering what's your AI product strategies and investment scale?
Operator
My second question is about VATP. Could you please share an update on the business development with your VATP license? Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign Language]。Uh, for, for VATP license, there's, uh, actually there's no any, you know, uh, update, uh, in the Q1, uh, despite, uh, we, we got, uh, the, the short list-
by Hong Kong SFC for VATP license alongside with other, a couple of applicants. Now we are still in the process of phase II. There are still a lot of validations need to be conducted by the third party, consultant, independent consultant. There's a lot of, you know, process testing work need to be complete in order to get the final approval from SFC. We will keep you posted for there's any progress. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
In terms of our AI strategy, Futu has assembled our own AI team. We're closely monitoring the industry developments and keeping up with innovations. The AI is applied in two ways at Futu. One internally, we use that to increase operating efficiency, and we also leverage AI to develop new products and features for our clients. In terms of operation efficiency, we've already leveraged AI in a number of scenarios, including customer services, the account opening, documentation, and verification processes, and we've seen AI bringing tangible uplifts to our operating efficiency.
In terms of our client-facing features, we think that for active traders, a key benefit of AI would be to lower the investment threshold and help them more efficiently gather information to make informed investment decisions. For example, we'll launch algo trading very soon. Before, algo trading is almost exclusively for the sophisticated institutional investors. Now for our retail clients, by telling AI the stock you are interested in, the parameters you wanna monitor, and what kind of conditions will trigger trade, our AI can generate an algo trading function for our clients, which we think significantly lower their barrier. Around that goal, we'll continue to innovate to bring more AI-powered features. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you for the questions. With that, I would like to hand the call back to Mr. Daniel Yuan for closing.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and Investor Relations, Futu Holdings
That concludes our call today. On behalf of the Futu management team, I would like to thank you for joining us today. If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact me or any of our investor relations representatives. Thank you and goodbye.
Operator
That concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign language]

Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
[Foreign language]
Daniel Yuan

Brokerage commission handling charge income was HKD 2.1 billion, an increase of 128% year-over-year and 35% quarter-over-quarter. Other income was HKD 353 million, up 157% year-over-year and 69% quarter-over-quarter. The year-over-year and the quarter-over-quarter increase was both primarily attributed to higher fund distribution income and the currency exchange income. Our total cost was HKD 776 million, an increase of 79% from HKD 434 million in Q4 2023. Brokerage commission and the handling charge expenses was HKD 112 million, up 90% year-over-year and 38% quarter-over-quarter. The quarter-over-quarter increase was roughly in line with the movement of our brokerage commission and the handling charge income. Interest expenses were HKD 513 million, up 19% year-over-year and 24% quarter-over-quarter.
The year-over-year increase was driven by higher interest expenses associated with our security borrowing and the lending business. The quarter-over-quarter increase was mainly due to higher margin financing interest expenses as a result of higher funding costs for Hong Kong dollars. Processing and the servicing costs were HKD 151 million, up 45% year-over-year and 16% quarter-over-quarter. The increase was largely due to higher market information and the data fee for new products with higher system usage fees. As a result, total gross profit was HKD 3.7 billion, an increase of 89% from HKD 1.9 billion in Q4 2023. Gross margin was 82.5% as compared to 81.7% in Q4 2023. As a result, income from operation increased 117% year-over-year and 28% quarter-over-quarter to HKD 2.2 billion.
Operating margin increased to 50% from 43.1% in Q4 2023, mostly due to strong top line growth and operating leverage. Our net income increased by 113% year-over-year and 42% quarter-over-quarter to HKD 1.9 billion. Net income margin expanded to 42.2% in the Q4 as compared to 36.9% in the same quarter last year. SVP, Futu Holdings

Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of Strategy and IR, Futu Holdings

Thank you.

Daniel Yuan

Well, that concludes our earnings call. On behalf of the Futu management team, I would like to thank you for joining us today. If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact me or any of our investor relations representatives. Thank you and goodbye.

第四季度，由于香港市场情绪低迷，本地获客速度放缓。但今年一季度，随着香港股市的复苏有所反弹。在美国，我们继续关注客户质量。新增有资产客户的户均首季度净入金环比增长约30%。在澳大利亚，我们专注于品牌建设以及产品上新，并于四季度上线了现金管理产品。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Client acquisition in Hong Kong slowed down due to sluggish market sentiments, yet rebounded in Q1 along with the recovery of the Hong Kong stock market. In the US, we continue to prioritize client quality over quantity, with the average asset balance of new paying clients in their first quarter of onboarding increasing by over 30% compared to the last quarter. In Australia, we focused on cultivating brand equity and adding new products, including cash management.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
今年的二月二十六日，我们在马来西亚正式上线了证券经纪服务。业务上线以来，获客势头强劲，上线一周内开户客户超过三万人。这是我们所有国际市场中增长最快的。过去三年，我们在新加坡的市占率增长迅猛，品牌影响力辐射范围广，所以我们从上线初期就在马来西亚积累了较高的知
On 26 February 2023, we launched brokerage business in Malaysia and gained significant traction. Over 30,000 clients flocked to our platform within 1 week of the official launch, representing the fastest growth in any of our international markets. We managed to generate high brand awareness in Malaysia from the outset, thanks to our rapid share gain in Singapore over the past 3 years.
今年我们在各个市场都看到了有资产客户强劲的增长势头。今年前两个月的净增有资产客户和净入金规模已经超过去年第四季度。鉴于今年至今为止的强劲势头，我们预计2024年净增35万名有资产客户。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
We observed robust paying client growth across all markets this year. In fact, we attracted more paying clients and net asset inflows in the first two months this year than the entire Q4. Given the strong momentum year to date, we are guiding for 350,000 net new paying clients in 2024.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
客户总资产同比增长16%，环比增长4%，达到4,860亿港元。环比增长主要得益于客户每股资产市值的上涨以及各个市场强劲的净入金。在新加坡，由于各个cohort客户入金都很强劲，客户总资产和平均资产分别环比增长25%和17%，户均资产超过1.7万新元。随着我们的品牌影响力的不断增强，moomoo得到了越来越多高净值人群的青睐。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Total client assets increased by 16% year over year and 4% quarter over quarter to HKD 486 billion. The sequential increase was largely due to robust net asset inflow across all regions, and the market appreciation of our clients' US stock holdings. In Singapore, total client assets and average client assets posted sequential increase of 25% and 17% respectively. Average client assets was over SGD 17,000 due to strong inflows across cohorts. As we continue to build brand equity, moomoo gained traction among high net worth clients in Singapore. As of quarter end, margin financing and securities lending balance increased marginally by 2% quarter over quarter. While we saw an uptick in securities lending balance for US stocks, margin financing balance declined as clients unwound their positions.
Total trading volume was HKD 957 billion, down 12% year-over-year and quarter over quarter. In Q4, Hong Kong and US stock trading volume were down 13% and 12% sequentially. Weak sentiments around Hong Kong equities and lower turnover in US tech stocks dragged total trading volume. Our share gains in the derivatives market in Hong Kong was a bright spot. Hong Kong futures and options trading had 8.5% and 14.7% market share in Q4, respectively. Next, I'd like to invite our CFO, Arthur, to discuss our financial performance.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Leaf and Daniel. Before going through our financial performance, I'd like to give you an update on our latest share repurchase program announced on 11 March 2022. As of 31 December 2023, the expiration day of the program, we had repurchased an aggregate of 11 million ADSs with approximately $365 million total repurchase amount in open market transactions. We have put in place a new share repurchase program which approves and authorizes to repurchase up to $500 million of ADSs before 31 December 2025. Now, please allow me to walk you through our financial performance. All numbers are in HKD unless otherwise noted. Total revenue was HKD 2.4 billion, up 4% from HKD 2.3 billion in Q4 2022.
We ended 2023 with full year revenue growing 31% to HKD 10 billion. Brokerage commission and handling charge income was HKD 904 million, a decrease of 14% year-over-year and 10% QoQ. The decrease was mainly driven by lower trading volume. Interest income was HKD 1.3 billion, up 17% year-over-year and down 11% QoQ. The year-over-year increase was mainly driven by high interest income from clients' cash deposits due to higher benchmark interest rate and higher margin financing income due to an increase in daily average margin balance. The QoQ decrease was mostly driven by the lower interest income from clients' cash deposits due to decrease in daily average client cash balance.
Other income was HKD 137 million, up 46% year-over-year and largely flat Q over Q. The year-over-year increase was primarily attributed to higher fund distribution income, partially offset by lower enterprise public relations service income and underwriting fee income. Our total costs were HKD 433 million, an increase of 27% from HKD 342 million in Q4 of 2022. Brokerage commission and handling charge expenses were HKD 59 million, down 8% year-over-year and 6% Q over Q. The decrease was roughly in line with our decrease in our brokerage commission and handling charge income, partially offset by the cost of migrating our SGX equities to our self-clearing system. Interest expenses were HKD 271 million, up 49% year-over-year and down 6% quarter-over-quarter.
The year-over-year increase was driven by high interest expenses associated with our security borrowing and the lending business, and the higher margin financing interest expenses. The quarter over quarter decrease was mostly due to lower interest expenses associated with our security borrowing and the lending business, partially offset by high margin financing interest expenses. Processing and servicing costs was HKD 104 million, up 7% year-over-year, and 21% quarter over quarter. The increase was largely due to higher product service fee for new markets and higher system usage fees. As a result, our total gross profit was HKD 1.9 billion, largely flat year-over-year. Gross margin was 81.7% as compared to 85% in Q4 2022. Operating expenses was up 12% year-over-year, and 3% quarter over quarter for HKD 916 million.
R&D expenses was $363 million, up 9% year-over-year, and 1% quarter over quarter. The year-over-year increase was mainly due to increasing R&D head count as we continue to support new product offerings in international markets. Selling and marketing expenses was $182 million, up 19% year-over-year, and down 14% quarter over quarter. The year-over-year increase was due to a 41% year-over-year increase in net new paying clients, partially offset by lower customer acquisition costs. The quarter over quarter decrease was due to few net new clients and the lower customer acquisition costs. G&A expenses was $317 million, up 12% year-over-year, and 15% quarter over quarter. The increase was primarily due to an increase in head count for general administrative personnel, partially offset by lower professional service fees.
As a result, income from operations decreased 9% year-over-year and 22% quarter-over-quarter to HKD 1 billion. Operating margin declined to 43.1% from 49.1% in Q4 2022, mostly due to operating deleverage. Our net income decreased by 9% year-over-year and 20% quarter-over-quarter to HKD 876 million. Net income margin shrank to 36.9% in Q4 as compared to 42% in the same quarter last year. Among our international business, Singapore was the first to achieve break-even on a quarterly basis, even with partial support from headquarters. As client assets continue to grow, we believe the unit economics in Singapore will maintain an upward trajectory. That concludes our prepared remarks. We'd now like to open the call to questions. Operator, please go ahead. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. To ask a question, you'll need to press star one and one on your telephone and wait for your name to be announced. To withdraw your question, please press star one and one again. Once again, that's star one and one to ask a question. Please stand by while we compile the Q&A, Russ. Thank you. We'll now take the first question. Please stand by. First question today is from the line of Cindy Wang from China Renaissance. Please go ahead.
Cindy Wang
Analyst and Director, China Renaissance
Thanks for taking my call, and I have two questions. First one is, what's your progress of improving account opening process in Japan? Could you provide more color on new paying clients acquisition in Q4 last year versus Q1 this year so far in Japan? When would you expect to launch Japan stock trading? The second question is regarding to the new paying clients. We see the new paying client target of 350,000 in 2024 is very impressive. Could you break down by key markets, including like Hong Kong, Singapore, US, Japan, et cetera? Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Cindy. I will take your second question first, and we'll leave the first question to my colleague, Daniel. In terms of our new targets for 2024, the contributions from Singapore, Hong Kong, and, you know, Australia in absolute terms should be similar to last year. The incremental growth drivers mainly come from certain new markets we enter into this year and recently in Q4 last year, such as Japan, Canada, and Malaysia. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Hi, Cindy, this is Daniel, and I'll take your question on Japan. In Q4, we continued to optimize the account opening process and to integrate the redundant processes and pages in that process and to iterate on the key friction points. We have seen therefore a very meaningful increase in the conversion rate from users to registered clients to paying clients. In comparison to other international markets, there is still a lot of room for improvement in that conversion number. To continue to optimize that account opening golden process will be a key priority for us this year. In terms of Japan equities trading, yes, we are planning to roll out Japan equities trading to our Japan clients by the end of March.
In April or May, we're gonna roll out Japan equities trading to our clients in Hong Kong and Singapore. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. We'll now take our next question. This is from the line of Chiyao Huang from Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.
Chiyao Huang
Research Analyst, Morgan Stanley
My question is on the Singapore. So what was roughly the client number and client asset contribution on the overall firm basis? And also wonder what's the strategy in Singapore for 2024, and how is the competitive landscape changing in Singapore? And also what's the, you know, risk appetite evolving for Singapore clients in 2024, given that the US market is still performing quite well? Are they trading more stocks? Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Chiyao. My colleague Robin will answer this question for you.
Robin Xu
SVP, Futu Holdings
Hello.
In Q4, Singapore recorded very steady client growth and contributed about 30% of our total net new clients for the entire quarter. Thanks to the continued net asset inflows of our existing clients and the higher quality new clients, the total client assets and average client assets in Singapore have recorded 25% and 17% sequential growth respectively. The total client assets have reported sequential increase for every single quarter since we launched the business. Average client assets have been on a upward trajectory for 6 consecutive quarters. As of the end of last year, average client assets in Singapore was over 17,000 SGD.
We believe that as we continue to enhance our brand awareness, to diversify and enrich our product offerings, and to improve our client services, Moomoo will continue to attract more high net worth individuals. We've also seen the unit economics in Singapore continue to improve in the past two years. Taking into account the cost from the headquarters to support Singapore, the Singapore subsidiary broke even for the first time during Q4. We have seen very good growth year to date. In terms of clients' risk appetite, during the past rate hike cycle, we started to promote our Cash Plus product, which is the money market fund product. We continue to cross-sell different investment products based on our clients' risk appetite.
This year we have seen very strong traction in US equities among our Singapore clients. Thank you.
Chiyao Huang
Research Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Thank you very much.
You Fan
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, CICC
Thank you. We'll now take our next question. This is from the line of You Fan from CICC. Please go ahead.
好的，谢谢管理层给我这个提问的机会，我是中金公司的分析师樊优。那我这边有两个问题想请教一下，首先第一个的话是关于这个综合的佣金率，那我们看到其实这个季度环比进一步还是有所提升的，想请教一下背后的原因。然后第二个问题是关于这个获客成本，看到其实这个季度整体的获客成本环比也是有比较明显的一个下降，也是想请教一下背后的原因，然后包括咱们后续各个这个新市场继续加大展业之后，怎么去展望未来的一个获客成本趋势。我这边快速翻译一下。My first question is regarding the blended commission rate.
We see the commission rate increase this quarter, so what's the reason behind? The second question is about the CAC. We see the CAC decrease a lot this quarter. What's the reason behind? And how do you view the future trend of the CAC?
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you. I will take these two questions. For commission rate, the combined take rate is almost flat on a QoQ basis, slightly up because of the product mixture and more contributions from our derivative products. Then for the CAC, we further optimize different, you know, marketing campaigns channels to control and even decrease our CAC, which bore very strong results in Q4. Looking forward and based on the year-to-date situations, we do expect this year the CAC number will decrease compared with last year, hopefully, by 10% to 20% year-on-year. Thank you.
You Fan
Executive Director and Equity Research Analyst, CICC
好的，谢谢，非常清楚。Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. We'll now take our next question. Please stand by. Next question is from the line of Emma Xu from Bank of America Securities. Please go ahead.
Emma Xu
Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America Securities
谢谢给我这个提问的机会。我这边也是有两个问题，第一个问题就是刚刚我们重点介绍的新加坡，就是客户的这个质量在持续的改善。那我想问一下，就是说其他的这几个主要的国际市场，我们的客户质量变化是怎样的？就是户均资产有没有也在改善呢？然后包括香港市场的话，随着我们更多地去获取这个线下客户，香港客户这边的……
那个客户画像或者这个整体的资产规模，平均资产规模有没有变化？然后第二个…… 喂，对，能听见吗？然后第二个问题是想问一下关于成交量的。就是，成交量的话，其实在四季度也跌到了一个，换手率也跌到了一个历史的低点。然后香港市场这个成交不活跃其实也比较理解，因为市场情况确实不好，但是美股的话，成交量也，这个看起来成交量也是有一个比较明显的下滑哈。但是其实美股四季度表现还可以，然后包括一季度美股也是有一个持续的很好的表现。所以就想问一下，我们应该去怎样思考这个，换手率和，市场表现的关系。然后一季度的话，我们是否看到了这个，换手率啊，成交量啊，从四季度的低点，有一个明显的反弹呢？
I have two questions. The first one is about the client quality in other international markets. You mentioned earlier about the positive progress in the Singapore client quality, but how about other international markets?
Do you also see improvement in the average client asset? For your Hong Kong market, with you penetrating into the mass market, how will the client profile and average client asset change? The second question is about your trading velocity and trading volume. The trading velocity declined to a record low in Q4, and it is quite understandable that the Hong Kong trading velocity declined due to the weak market. However, US market actually performed quite well in the Q4, but your US trading volume also declined. How should we think about the connection between the market performance and your trading volume and your trading velocity? Do we see a notable rebound of your trading velocity in Q1?
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you. I will take your second question first and leave the first question to my colleague Daniel. In terms of trading velocity, you are right. The trading velocity is down in Hong Kong and the US, in Q4. Despite the US stocks performed very well, in Q4, but it remains a very strong, continuous uptrend, for the whole quarters. Most of our clients actually use a buy-and-hold strategy to enjoy the rallies.
The implied volatility in the US markets, in Q4 actually, went down, compared with Q3. The trading velocities, you know, decrease, actually, you know, based on our humble observations, is in line with a lot of other US discount brokers' operating metrics as well. In the first quarter this year, so far, we have seen a very healthy pickup, not only in the US, but also in Hong Kong in terms of the trading volume and also the trading velocity. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Emma. This is Daniel, and I will take your question on the client quality in international markets.
Actually, we have seen an improvement in average AUM, not only in Singapore, but also in our other international markets, including the US, Australia, and Japan. Mostly because, unlike some of our other peers, I think Futu really cares about quality growth. Net inflow of AUM is a key KPI, very important KPI for all of our marketing teams across different international regions. In Q4, we have seen very strong AUM inflows despite weak market sentiments. In the first two months this year, as Leaf mentioned in his opening remarks, we have a higher net asset inflow in the first two months of this year than the entire Q4 combined. Actually, over one-third of that net asset inflow comes from international markets.
We'll expect a continued upward trajectory in our client assets across international markets. For Hong Kong, in the past couple of quarters, we continued to attract older clients, especially with our offline store. We have seen that these clients typically have higher average assets. Because of the large base effect, these new clients didn't change the overall client profile much in Hong Kong. Thank you.
Emma Xu
Director and Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America Securities
Thank you. This is really encouraging.
Operator
Thank you. We'll now take our next question. This is from the line of Leon Qi from Daiwa. Please go ahead.
Leon Qi
Regional Head of Asia Financials, FinTech, and HealthTech Research, Daiwa Capital Markets
好的，非常感谢给我这个提问的机会。我是Leon Qi。有两个问题想请教一下管理层。首先是在我们这个香港的营销策略上，因为刚才讲新加坡讲的比较多了，刚才也听到管理层讲这个新的有资产客户的指引上面，就是明年香港新增的有资产客户是跟这个……
就2024年是跟2023年差不多的。那么随着我们香港现有的这个有资产客户的基数越来越大，不知道管理层会不会这个逐渐把这个业务经营上面的重点，从获客数一点点转向客均资产，就想了解一下这个，管理层在这方面是怎么样打算的。第二个呢是想请教一下我们美股，这个我知道我们技术上已经是可以自清算了，但实际上，是不是美股完全都已经自清算了。我们自清算之后，除了对于我们净利收入的帮助之外，对于我们的这个交易效率，是不是有提高？不知道这方面是不是有一些美国的同业，可以给我们对比，比如说像Interactive Brokers这一些。好，我这个用英文翻译一下。Thanks for taking my questions.
This is Leon Qi. I wanna ask two questions today. Firstly is on our Hong Kong marketing and client acquisition strategy. Just now management shared a lot of details on Singapore, but I'm interested in Hong Kong now. Given we have an increasing number of client base, paying client base now, would management feel that going forward, it will be increasingly more difficult for us to acquire new customers? Are we considering gradually shifting our focus from the number of customers into average AUM or the quality of our customers? We do appreciate the new customer guidance that management talked about just now, that Hong Kong new customers guidance in 2024 would be similar to 2023.

In addition to the positive impact on our net interest income, do we see any improvement in terms of our trading execution efficiencies by using self-clearing? Wondering if we can make any comparisons with our competitors in the US such as Interactive Brokers, et cetera. Thank you very much.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Leon. I'll let Lee to take the first question, and I will answer the second one.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
感谢提问。我来回答那个关于香港的问题。香港市场是我们的大本营。2023年我们在香港的年轻人群体当中，持续保持着一个非常高的渗透率。我们在其他年龄段的人口渗透率也在稳步的提升。那么截止到第四季度，富途在香港35到55岁人群中的有资产客户渗透率已经超过了10%。在香港市场，我们的目标是高质量的增长，我们着重获取高质量客户，并且针对存量客户去做精细化的运营。因此在市场行情疲软的时候，我们会在净入金方面依然能看到它是保持着一个非常强劲的势头。未来我们会更好地去利用富途在全品类的优势，去延续对不同的资产量级和投资需求的人群，去做分层运营的策略，并且会持续去关注净入金的趋势。谢谢。
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
The Hong Kong market is our home base, and in 2023, we continue to maintain very high penetration among the younger clients. We also steadily improve our penetration into clients from other age groups. As of the end of Q4, our paying client penetration among the adults aged 35 to 55 in Hong Kong was over 10%. In Hong Kong, our goal is to achieve high quality growth, and we focus on acquiring high quality clients and also focus on attracting net asset inflow from existing clients. That's why, during Q4 and also in the past, where market sentiments were weak. We continue to see very robust net asset inflow from Hong Kong. Going forward, we'll leverage our comprehensive product offerings and have different operational strategies for clients with different asset amount and different investment needs.
We'll very closely track the net asset inflow trend in Hong Kong. Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
For the second question, you are right. We have already largely completed the US self-clearing so far. I think actually the positive contributions from this migration will continue thanks to the increase in the client asset cohort and also the contributions from the new markets, such as Japan and Malaysia. In terms of the operating efficiency, definitely, you know, after the self-clearing capabilities, our service downtime versus before has been meaningfully decreased. Also the trading execution in terms of the reporting, et cetera, will be more smooth. Thank you.
Leaf Li
Chairman and CEO, Futu Holdings
Thank you very much.
Operator
Thank you. As a reminder, if you would like to ask a question, you can press star one and one on your keypad. We will now take our next question. Please stand by. The next question is from the line of Peter Zhang from JPMorgan. Please go ahead.
Peter Zhang
Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan Chase & Co.
谢谢管理层给我提问的问题。
提问的机会。我是摩根大通的Peter。我的第一个问题是关于利息收入，这个季度利息收入环比有所下降。我想请教一下管理层，背后的原因是什么？管理层分别讲解一下客户闲置资金的情况，还有我们利率的一些零存款利率的一个趋势。然后我想问一下，一季度以来我们客户的闲置资金余额的情况的最新的变动趋势是如何的？第二个问题，我是想问一下关于成本端的。我想问一下，管理层对于2024年我们增员的headcount的一个情况，有没有一个指引？然后管理层对于我们2024年成本端的增长，还有成本收入比的一个变化，有没有一个指引？我翻译一下。
Uh, my first question is about interest income. We noticed that interest income had been decreased sequentially in Q1. We wish to understand what's the Q4 trends for clients idle cash and Futu's deposit rates. And I also wish to understand what's the trend in Q1 for clients idle cash balance. My second question is about operating expense. I wish to understand what's Futu's plan for the headcount increase in 2024, and what's management's guidance for Futu's operating expense increase or, say, cost-to-income ratio trend. Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Peter. I will take these two questions. For idle cash, roughly the idle cash accounts for 10% to 15% of our total client assets in the past quarter. The similar situations happened in Q1 so far. The decrease of the interest revenue in Q4, as I mentioned in the opening remarks, is mainly due to the decrease of the average balance for the security borrowing and the lending. Despite if you see the balance sheet data, the margin and the security lending balance was higher than that in Q3. For the second half of your questions, in terms of headcount, we are looking for mid- to high-single-digit headcount growth.
Mainly, we'll be deployed for our international market expansion and to further enhance our R&D capabilities. Unfortunately, we do not have a cost-income ratio guidance. Given the nature of our business, our revenue is very volatile, is very difficult to predict due to the market volatility. We were more focusing on the people side, given this is one of the largest, you know, cost components for our overall cost structure. Thank you.
Peter Zhang
Equity Research Analyst, JPMorgan Chase & Co.
谢谢，非常清楚。Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. This does conclude the question and answer session. At this time, I would like to hand the conference back to Daniel Yuan for closing remarks. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to the CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
That concludes our call today. On behalf of the Futu management team, I would like to thank you for joining us today. If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact me or any of our investor relations representatives. Thank you and goodbye.
Operator
Thank you. This does conclude today's conference call. Thank you for participating, and you may now disconnect.

Besides U.S. stock trading commission, we also intend to monetize over margin financing and foreign exchange fees. We observe that Japanese investors really like to trade on margin. We have seen that in the industry average number, like around 50% of their trades are placed with margin. That's gonna be a key revenue driver. For FX charges, we understand that in order to compensate for zero commission for Japanese stock trading, all of the brokers in Japan charge pretty hefty fees for FX.
As the trading volume of U.S. stock trading on our platform grows, we also expect FX revenue to make a meaningful contribution. Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you very much.
Operator
Thank you. Next question comes from the line of Cindy Wang with China Renaissance. Please go ahead.
Cindy Wang
Analyst, China Renaissance
Hi. Thanks for taking my question. I have two questions. First one is related to Japan market. Can you share the coverage of Japan's maintaining clients' progress? What's the conversion rate from registered users to paying clients? Have you seen maintaining clients increasing month-over-month? Second question is for the PantherTrade applying for digital assets trading platform in Hong Kong. What is the progress with that? What is your preparation work for digital assets trading platform? Would you be able to launch trading functions immediately once their license is approved? Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
Thank you, Cindy. I will answer your second question first, and my colleague Daniel will answer your question regarding Japan. We echo the Web3 policies advocated by the Hong Kong government, who want to build up Hong Kong as a Web3 global center. In the past several quarters, we carefully studied the policies and the regulations issued by Hong Kong SFC.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
PantherTrade, a wholly subsidiary within Futu Group, submitted that VASP license application to Hong Kong SFC last month, and we expect the whole application process may take at least six to nine months, when if we have the luck to get approval in principle. We have not formed a very concrete business plans afterwards, and we will continue to modify this content in the next couple of quarters, and hopefully we can give some new updates in next Q2 or Q3. Thank you.
谢谢Cindy。我来take第一个关于日本的问题。那目前在日本市场，我们从用户到开户客户，然后从开户客户到入金客户的转化率都要比我们其他的国际市场要低一些。那我们觉得主要目前有两个原因吧。第一个原因是可能在我们的开户的这个黄金流程上，我们觉得还是有一些friction points的。那因为目前在日本证券行业的中后台还是涉及了不少体验参差的一些外包的系统，那我们为了尽快可以给客户提供这个开户的能力，其实采用了一些行业通行的一些安排，那这个对用户体验是有一定的负面影响的。那我们未来一段时间会重点去优化开户入金的这个黄金流程，然后在之后几个季度逐渐将这个流程中的一些外包的环节替代为我们自研的这个系统。那另外一个我们觉得造成这个转化率偏低的原因是，就是我们品类上的一些缺失吧。那目前像刚才提到的只上线了美股正股的交易，那我们预计明年一季度可以上线日股的交易和这个NISA账户的能力。那虽然我们相信富途的这个美股交易能力在日本的市场中是遥遥领先的，但是目前在日本，日股依旧是本地投资者非常重要的一个交易的标的。那我们是希望我们之后在当地市场推广的时候，品类也是比较完善的。所以根据我们对目前用户的一些调研，我们理解这个也是阻碍部分用户在我们这开户入金的一个原因吧。
I'm gonna translate for myself. Right now in Japan, the user to client conversion rate as well as the client to paying client conversion rate are both lower than what we have observed in other international markets. We think there are two main reasons behind it. Number one is that our account opening onboarding process still has a number of friction points. So far, the mid- to back-office in the Japanese brokerage industry are still characterized by a lot of outsourced systems that have really unsatisfactory user experience. In order to start account opening soon, we leverage some of these outsourced systems, which really have a negative impact on our users' experience, and thus impacted the conversion rate from account opening to asset deposits. In next couple of quarters, we plan to invest into our account opening process and gradually replace these outsourced systems with our proprietary system. The second reason behind this low conversion rate so far is the lack of key trading products. As mentioned earlier, we now only offer U.S. cash equities trading to Japan users. In Q1 next year, we plan to launch Japanese stock trading as well as NISA account. Although we are really confident that Futu's U.S. stock trading capabilities lead our Japanese peers by a very wide margin. In Japan, the Japanese stock investing is still very, very popular. We understand based on our user survey that lack of, you know, Japanese equity trading is a key reason that prevents them from opening accounts with us. Thank you.
Operator
Ms. Wang, are you done with your question?
Cindy Wang
Analyst, China Renaissance
Yes.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Yes, I am done, thank you.
Cindy Wang
Analyst, China Renaissance
It's okay. Thank you.
Operator
Thank you. A reminder to all the participants that you may press star and one to ask a question. Next question comes from the line of Peter Zhang with JP Morgan. Please go ahead.
Peter Zhang
Analyst, JPMorgan
谢谢管理层给我提供的机会。我对于日本这边我还是有一个follow-up的问题，我想问一下，在未来有没有机会，就是我们香港或者新加坡的用户可以去交易日股，就是在我们的product pipeline上有没有这个考虑？然后第二个问题是，就是这个季度交易的那个佣金费率环比有所下降，我想问一下背后的原因以及未来的趋势会如何？
Okay, let me do the translation. My first question is a follow-up question regarding the Japan product line. I wish to understand, going forward, will Futu's clients in Hong Kong or Singapore market be allowed to trade Japan stock? Is this product in your product pipeline? My second question is regarding the blended commission fee rate. We notice that the blended commission fee rate declined sequentially in Q3, and we wish to understand what's the reason behind, and what will be the trend going forward. Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
好的，谢谢 Peter。我来回答你的这两个问题。第一个是有关这个日本的股票交易会不会这个功能在其他的这些市场里面提供。那我们的答案是确定的，而且这已经在我们的相应的产品排期的相应的一个管线里面。我相信这个对于日本以外的其他的一些交易者的获取，包括他们的留存，以及对于我们的收入，都会有一个非常正面的帮助。
那么第二个问题有关于我们三季度的佣金费率环比的小幅下降，这个原因呢，我们在之前其实好几个季度也有解释过，主要的原因是我们的美股交易的收费，是有两种不同的收费套餐，一种呢是按照百分比来收取，还有一种呢是按照股票的数量来收取。所以呢，客户在每个季度交易的股票的面值，交易的大面值的股票跟小面值股票的一个比例，会影响到我们综合的佣金费率，影响在这个里面。所以这个季度的佣金费率环比的小幅下降，也是因为市场的原因在这个里面。那么展望未来的情况，我们目前对于整体的综合佣金费率的稳定，还是保持一个比较乐观的状态。Regarding two questions.
Number one is for the Japan stock trading offering to the markets outside of Japan. Our answer is definitely it would be a yes and has already been in our product pipelines. Hopefully we can launch the U.S., the Japan stock trading to our clients in Hong Kong and Singapore in the near future. We do think this kind of product offering will further helpful to our client engagement in these markets and also increase the clients participation in our platform. Our top line will also benefit arising from that.
Regarding the blended commission rate fluctuation, as we elaborate to the market several quarters, it is mainly due to the clients' trading behaviors, because our U.S. stock trading commissions do have different menus, price menus, and one menu is actually not based on the percentage of the trading volume, but on the number of the shares. When people trade these big blue chips or these, you know, OTC stocks, the combination will have the implications on the blended commission rate as well. In the third quarter, the fluctuation is mainly because of that. Going forward, we think, you know, the blended commission rate if we take out this trading patterns reasons can maintain stable in the near future. Thank you.
Peter Zhang
Analyst, JPMorgan
谢谢，非常非常非常感谢。
Operator
Thank you. Next question comes from the line of Li Wan with BOCOM International. Please go ahead.
Li Wan
Analyst, BOCOM International
感谢给我提问的机会。我想请教一个关于利息收入的问题。就是整个今年您收入的增长，利息收入贡献比较大，那能否给我们拆解一下，比如说融资融券和银行存款的贡献都分别是多少？然后如果明年美联储降息的话，会对我们收入的增速是一个怎样的影响？我翻译一下。Can you give us a breakdown of interest income and what will be the impact from Fed's rate cut next year?
Thank you.
Arthur Chen
CFO, Futu Holdings
好的，有关利息收入的这个问题我来回答一下。整体我们的这个利息收入里面，客户的闲置资金的这个利息收入的占比，贡献在今年的这个占比贡献是要高于融资融券的，这个利息的收入。那么往前看，我们觉得整个的美联储减息的速度会是一个非常缓慢的状态。那么同时呢，在美联储减息的时候，虽然我们的利息收入会受到一定负面的影响，但是联储的这个减息在同一个情况下也会刺激整体的资本市场的活跃程度。那从以往去看，在减息的这个周期里面，客户参与市场的交易活跃度，包括交易量，都会有相应的上升。在一定程度上，交易收入的上升会弥补掉我们客户的闲置利息收入的下降。 In terms of the interest income, the interest revenues contributed from the client idle cash is much bigger than the interest income derived from the margin lending and the security lending business. Going forward, we do not think the Fed's rate cut will be very fast. In circumstances when the rate cut normally it would be helpful to the trading volumes for the whole capital markets, for our clients as well. Therefore, we do think the trading revenues arising from this rate cut will largely offset the potential idle cash revenue decrease. Thank you.
Operator
Ms. Wan, are you done with your question?
Li Wan
Analyst, BOCOM International
Yes, thank you.
Operator
Thank you. Next question comes from the line of Emma Xu with BofA Securities. Please go ahead. Miss Emma Xu, can you go ahead with your question?
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Well, it seems that Emma is not here tonight. Operator, do you have any further questions on the line?
Operator
There are no more questions. I will now hand the call back over to Mr. Yuan for closing comments. Thank you.
Daniel Yuan
Chief of Staff to CEO and Head of IR, Futu Holdings
Sure. Yeah. That concludes our call today. On behalf of the Futu management team, I would like to thank you for joining us today. If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact me or any of our investor relations representatives. Thank you, and goodbye.
Operator
Thank you. This concludes our conference for today. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
